title: CoFounder
humanEdge: Build the commercial engine for AI development. As CoFounder, you drive revenue by closing enterprise clients, then coordinate their builds with our network of expert builders. You shape product offerings, pricing strategy, and partnership models that scale across the AI development market.
summary: SkyHunter is seeking a CoFounder to build and lead the business development function. You will own the complete sales cycle—from qualifying enterprise prospects through contract close—then coordinate delivery with our technical partners. Your success directly determines company growth. You are not managing salespeople; you are the salesperson, and you are establishing a repeatable, scalable go-to-market model that other founders will eventually join. This role requires entrepreneurial DNA, sales discipline, and the ability to learn the technical landscape deeply enough to build trust with CIOs and CTOs seeking AI solutions.
responsibilities: Lead outbound prospecting to identify enterprises and startups building with AI or wanting to integrate AI into existing products. Target companies with $10M+ revenue and technical teams, focusing on verticals where AI adds clear competitive advantage (e-commerce, legal tech, healthcare, financial services).

Close deals: move prospects through discovery → technical qualification → business case → contract signature. You own the relationship and negotiate terms. Expected close rate: 15-20% of qualified opportunities, deal sizes $50K–$500K+.
Partner with builders: once a deal closes, brief technical partners on scope, timeline, and success metrics. Manage delivery milestones, client expectations, and quality gates. Escalate risks early.

Establish business model: define service tiers, pricing strategies, and partner economics. Build repeatable processes for scoping, quoting, and contracting. Document what works so the function can scale beyond you.

Develop partnerships and channels: build relationships with agencies, resellers, and strategic partners who can refer leads or co-sell with you. Establish SkyHunter as the trusted AI studio in your vertical.
Contribute to company strategy: input on product positioning, service offerings, and long-term vision. You represent the market voice internally.
broughtFrom: Required: 5+ years of enterprise software sales, demonstrated ability to close deals above $50K, and proven success in a founder or early-stage leadership role. You understand sales funnels, pipeline management, and how to forecast accurately. You bring strong networks in your target verticals. Nice to have: startup equity experience, knowledge of AI/LLM space, experience building business models from scratch. You are self-motivated, coachable, and comfortable with rejection and iteration.

title: Recruiter
humanEdge: Own the hiring function for a growing AI development studio. You build a talent pipeline of world-class engineers, designers, and product managers who want to ship real AI applications. You directly impact what kind of team and culture SkyHunter becomes.
summary: SkyHunter is building the team that shapes the future of AI development. We need a Recruiter who can identify, attract, and close top-tier technical talent—people who have shipped production AI/LLM applications or have deep relevant expertise. You will manage the full hiring cycle for engineering, design, and product roles. This means sourcing (building pipelines, not just posting jobs), screening (understanding technical depth and cultural fit), coordinating interviews, closing offers, and establishing relationships with talent who might not be ready to move now but could be in 6 months. Your success is measured by: hires made, time-to-close, quality of hires (retention and impact), and the strength of your pipeline.
responsibilities: Build and maintain sourcing pipeline: identify candidates through GitHub, Twitter, newsletters, referral networks, and direct outreach. Build relationships with potential candidates before there is an open role. Aim to maintain 50+ qualified prospects in different stages of engagement.

Screen for technical depth: conduct phone screens that assess not just experience but actual technical understanding. You should be able to have a basic technical conversation with engineers. Understand what good looks like in your target roles.

Manage candidate experience: coordinate all interviews (technical, culture, design), schedule with hiring managers, gather feedback, and communicate progress transparently. Candidates who don't get an offer should still feel respected and want to refer friends.

Close offers: when there is an offer, own the negotiation and close. Address objections, clarify terms, and get the candidate excited to join. Track offer-to-acceptance rates and improve your close rate.
Build team culture: help shape what kind of people we hire. Contribute to interview rubrics, onboarding, and cultural values. Recruit people who will grow and stay.
Develop recruiting strategy: analyze what roles we need most, what markets are competitive, what sourcing channels work best, and where talent gaps exist. Adapt strategy quarterly.
broughtFrom: Required: 3+ years of technical recruiting, proven ability to hire engineers or designers in competitive markets, and a strong network in tech/startup communities. You understand the difference between a referral, a network tap, and cold outreach. Nice to have: experience recruiting for AI/ML roles, founder mindset, track record of building recruiting processes from scratch. You are data-driven, scrappy, and genuinely excited about growing teams.

title: Agent Build Partner (Overflow Work)
humanEdge: Ship production AI agents and LLM applications for real clients with well-defined scope and clear deliverables. Work on your own schedule with projects that pay $2.5K–$6K per engagement. SkyHunter vets clients and specs projects so you get paid for quality work, not endless revisions.
summary: SkyHunter Partners is a curated network of AI builders taking on overflow client work. We vet clients and write detailed specifications so you know exactly what to build before you start. Projects typically take 2–6 weeks and pay $2.5K–$6K depending on scope. Examples: a customer support agent for an e-commerce company, a RAG system for a law firm to search case law, a data processing agent for a healthcare startup, a content generation agent for a marketing team. You claim projects that fit your expertise and schedule, deliver working code with documentation, and get paid. No long-term commitment, no endless meetings.
responsibilities: Browse available projects and claim ones that fit your expertise and availability. Projects are pre-specified with clear requirements, success criteria, and deliverables.
Work with the client via a kickoff call to clarify requirements and timelines. Ask clarifying questions upfront to avoid scope creep.

Build production-ready code: write clean, well-tested, documented code that a client can run and modify without you. Use best practices (error handling, logging, environment variables, README). Code reviews happen before payment.
Deliver on time: respect the agreed schedule. Communicate blockers early. If you hit a technical snag, tell the PM within 24 hours, not on delivery day.
Write handoff documentation: include setup instructions, dependencies, how to test locally, how to deploy, and what each component does. A non-technical person should be able to follow your README.
Be available for 30–60 minutes of post-delivery support: answer questions about your code, help with deployment issues, clarify intent if something is unclear. Beyond that is scope creep.
broughtFrom: Required: shipped at least one production LLM application that is actually used. Hands-on experience with Claude API or OpenAI's APIs, Python or TypeScript, and git. You write clean code and documentation. Nice to have: evaluation frameworks, prompt engineering, vector databases, web frameworks (FastAPI, Next.js). You are professional, deadline-conscious, and reliable.
